messages.subject: mixedmirt() with the bifactor model
parts:
Hi Phil,

First off, thank you for putting together and maintaining such a great psychometrics package - it really is a hugely useful tool for grad students. 

I am trying to build a longitudinal IRT model, incorporating some fixed effects. I was planning to use the mixedmirt() function and the lr.fixed and lr.random inputs. However, it does not appear that I can fit a bifactor model using the mixedmirt() function. Is that right? Is there no way to fit a bifactor model via the mixedmirt() function? Is there some other way I could fit a longitudinal bifactor model with fixed effects?

Thanks,
Charlie

Hi Charlie,

Thank you for the kind words.

On Tue, Dec 13, 2016 at 7:37 PM, Charlie_Rutgers <charles.i...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

First off, thank you for putting together and maintaining such a great psychometrics package - it really is a hugely useful tool for grad students. 

I am trying to build a longitudinal IRT model, incorporating some fixed effects. I was planning to use the mixedmirt() function and the lr.fixed and lr.random inputs. However, it does not appear that I can fit a bifactor model using the mixedmirt() function. Is that right? Is there no way to fit a bifactor model via the mixedmirt() function? Is there some other way I could fit a longitudinal bifactor model with fixed effects?

Yes you can fit a bifactor model with mixedmirt, just define the loadings pattern with the usual mirt.model() syntax and feed that into the model input. 

I'd worry a bit about having too many factors though, because the MH-RM algorithm will break at some point if too many random variables are included (you may need to tune the MH draws if they don't seem to be behaving correctly). Cheers.
 

Thanks,
Charlie
